title: Taichung vs Tainan: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Tainan for culture, street food, and 400 years of history. Taichung for modern city life, MRT transit, and Sun Moon Lake day trips. Do both if you have 7+ days in Taiwan.

categories.name: Street Food
categories.summary: Tainan is Taiwan's undisputed street food capital. Coffin bread, danzai noodles, and oyster vermicelli were invented here.

categories.name: History & Culture
categories.summary: Tainan is Taiwan's oldest city with Dutch forts, 1,600+ temples, and 400 years of history on every street.

categories.name: Public Transit
categories.summary: Taichung has an MRT; Tainan does not. Both have buses and YouBike but Taichung is easier to navigate.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Taichung has more bars, clubs, and night markets. Tainan has atmospheric Shennong Street craft beer scene but quieter overall.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Taichung is the gateway to Sun Moon Lake, Hehuanshan alpine road, Cingjing Farm, and Lukang old town.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Tainan is slightly cheaper, mainly due to the ubiquitous affordable street food. Both are much cheaper than Taipei.

categories.name: Weather
categories.summary: Taichung has more moderate year-round weather. Tainan wins in winter specifically (Oct-Feb).

categories.name: English Friendliness
categories.summary: Taichung has a larger expat community and more English speakers. Tainan works well if you know some Mandarin.

faq.question: Is Taichung or Tainan better for first-time visitors to Taiwan?
faq.answer: Depends on priorities. Tainan for authentic culture and food; Taichung for transit, nightlife, and day trips. Many itineraries do both (50 min apart by HSR).

faq.question: Which city has better street food?
faq.answer: Tainan wins convincingly — it's Taiwan's street food capital with coffin bread, danzai noodles, oyster vermicelli and more invented here.
